Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

sRtr (development version)

  • srtr_normalize_missing() is rebuilt on missing_codes. It recognises codes by what they mean in each variable’s own format, for raw codes and labelled columns alike, and a policy chooses which kinds become NA: "analysis" (the default), "strict" or "tag_only". actions changes the policy by kind and overrides by variable. reason = "changed" adds a _MISS column recording why each value became NA. Also new: output = "append", na_level, extra_codes, cols, file_key and release.

    Changes from the earlier version:

    • The missing_vals list and replacement are removed. Use extra_codes for your own codes and na_level for an explicit “Missing” level.
    • Raw codes of formatted variables are now recognised; before, most were recognised only after labelling.
    • 59 more variables are normalized by default, because their format has an unknown, not-done or pending code that the earlier list did not include (93 code meanings in 64 variables in all).
    • Not done and not tested still become NA by default; actions = c(not_done = "keep") keeps them (#28).
    • The internal list of default missing codes (R/sysdata.rda) is gone; everything it held is in missing_codes, where it can be read.

  • New srtr_missing_report() counts, for each variable, the values that stand for missing information and of which kind (unknown, not done, not applicable, …), using missing_codes. It changes nothing in the data, gives the same counts for raw codes and labelled columns, and reports values that are already NA and values a format does not list separately. detail = "code" lists every classified code with its count, to check the classification against the data (#28).

  • New dataset missing_codes: each SRTR format code that may stand for missing information, classified by what it means (unknown, not applicable, not done, pending, cannot disclose, indeterminate, partly known, SAS missing, or an ordinary value). The same code number means different things in different formats, so the classification is by format and code. A second table, variables, lists the raw values (blank, ND, U and similar) of flag columns that have no format; these come from the list srtr_normalize_missing() has used so far and are not documented in the SRTR dictionary. Nothing uses the dataset yet; srtr_normalize_missing() is unchanged (#27).

  • New dataset optn_mapping_tables: the OPTN KDRI-to-KDPI (2010 onward) and EPTS (2014 onward) mapping tables, parsed from OPTN’s PDFs, with each source file’s address and sha256, and the date each table took effect in allocation (#171, #172).

  • sRtr now needs R 4.1.0 or later and dplyr 1.1.0 or later, and no longer depends on magrittr. Package code calls every function as pkg::fun() (#55).

  • The cohort-building vignette now uses the CRAN package flowchart instead of strobe, and is renamed “Building Cohorts with Flow Diagrams” (#69).

  • Errors, warnings and messages now come from cli, so they are formatted consistently, and errors name the function you called. Every condition signalled by sRtr itself has a class you can catch: a general one (sRtr_error, sRtr_warning, sRtr_message) and a specific one such as sRtr_error_file_not_found or sRtr_error_missing_columns. Errors that come from base R or other packages, such as an invalid choice for an argument, keep their own classes. sRtr now imports cli (#102, #103).

  • formats: four code meanings (three in BILICOMP, one in DGN) showed a control character where SRTR’s page has an en dash or an apostrophe. The dictionary page is now read as Windows-1252, the encoding it uses, so they show the intended character (#26).

  • Loading sRtr no longer warns when SRTR_WD is not set, and no longer sets options(arrow.skip_nul = TRUE) for the session (#62).

  • The bundled dictionary now names the original MELD exception tumors file MPEXCEPT_ORIG_TUMORS, as the SRTR data file is named, instead of the shortened MPEXCEPT_ORIG_TUMO, so loading and labeling that file find its dictionary entries.

  • add_donor_egfr() is a new function that adds a donor’s eGFR from the CKD-EPI 2021 equation, or the 2009 equation for comparison with older work (#173).

  • add_epts() is a new function that adds the raw EPTS and the EPTS score for adult kidney candidates at listing or at transplant, using the mapping table of your choice (#172).

  • add_kdpi() is a new function that adds KDRI and KDPI for deceased kidney donors, with the refit formula OPTN has used since October 2024 or the original Rao 2009 formula, and the mapping table of your choice (#171).

  • add_lkdpi() is a new function that adds the Living Kidney Donor Profile Index for living donor kidney transplants (#178).

  • add_pdri() is now exported (#50).

  • add_pvr() is a new function that adds pulmonary vascular resistance from the catheterization values recorded at listing or at transplant (#179).

  • add_txf_outcomes() no longer fails unless dplyr is attached (#17).

  • apply_srtr_factors() and apply_srtr_varlabels() no longer fail when called as sRtr::fun() without sRtr attached (#90).

  • apply_srtr_factors() and apply_srtr_varlabels() now set a file_key attribute on their result, so a chain such as TX_KI |> apply_srtr_factors() |> apply_srtr_varlabels() labels both steps. file_key is matched in upper case. A key that is not in the bundled dictionary, or that cannot be worked out, now gives a warning instead of silently returning unlabeled data (#89).

  • apply_srtr_factors(), and so load_srtr_file() with its default factor_labels = TRUE, no longer turns values into NA (#15):

    • Ages with an age-band format (REC_AGE_AT_TX, CAN_AGE_AT_LISTING) stay numeric; before, every age that was not a band’s lower bound became NA. range_formats = "bin" bands them instead.
    • A value not listed in a format with a catch-all entry gets the catch-all label, as in SAS: race code 24 (White and Black) becomes “Multi-Racial”. other = "keep" turns this off.
    • Any other value not listed in its format is kept as its own level, named "<code>: not in format" so it cannot be mistaken for a label, with a warning; unknown_codes = "na" or "error" choose otherwise.
    • Calling it again on its own result changes nothing, and attributes on each column, such as a variable label, are kept.

  • load_srtr_file(), set_srtr_wd(), apply_srtr_factors() and apply_srtr_varlabels() gain a release argument, so a file is labelled with the SRTR data dictionary of the SAF release it comes from. The release can also come from a folder named like pubsaf2609; with none, the bundled dictionary and formats are used as before. A release between two stored dictionary versions uses the entries that are the same in both, and decides the rest from the file’s columns (gaps says what to do when an entry changed). The release and dictionary used are recorded in the srtr_release attribute (#26).

  • srtr_dictionary() returns the dictionary or format code lists for a SAF release, from the new dictionary_versions dataset of stored SRTR dictionary versions (#26).

  • calculate_geography_coverage_gain() now does what its arguments say (#58):

    • method = "centroid" and method = "areal" are implemented. Before, every method gave intersection results. The default is "areal".
    • output = "wide" returns one row with <variable>_<measure> columns.
    • geography_id adds a covered_ids attribute listing the geographies counted in each area.
    • All inputs are transformed to crs first.
    • It no longer fails unless dplyr and sf are attached (#55).

  • load_srtr_file() finds the folder set with set_srtr_wd() when it first needs it, and looks again if a file is not found, so files added during a session are picked up. Errors now say when SRTR_WD is not set and which folder was searched (#62).

  • load_srtr_file() col_select now works as documented (#98):

    • Tidyselect expressions such as starts_with("REC_") work; before, they failed before any file was read. Parquet files now get the selection too.
    • Names are matched in upper case, as in the result, and columns come back in the order selected.
    • trr_id_filter works when TRR_ID is not selected; it is read for the filter and then dropped.
    • A "TX_KP" subset no longer needs TFL_LAFUDATEKI and TFL_LAFUDATEPA. TFL_LAFUDATE can be selected by name, and is still added when both dates are selected.

  • load_srtr_file() now compares a file’s columns with the bundled data dictionary when every column is read. It warns about columns the file is missing and names columns the dictionary does not list (once per file per session). The new column_check argument turns the warning into an error ("error") or skips the comparison ("none") (#4).

  • rank_individual_coverage_gains() now defaults to method = "areal", like calculate_geography_coverage_gain() (#58).

  • srtr_composite_death() now requires its three death date columns to be Date, which is how load_srtr_file() returns SAS date columns, and errors with the names of any that are not. It no longer converts numbers or text to dates, so the parse argument is removed; the conversion could misread MM/DD/YYYY text and SAS day counts (#23, #59). A missing column now gives a clear error instead of a failed stopifnot().

  • srtr_normalize_missing() keeps the order of factor levels and removes only the replaced missing codes from them, so the reference level no longer depends on which value comes first in the data. Ordered factors and variable labels are kept (#20).

  • srtr_normalize_missing() now recognizes the default unknown codes of 18 variables it used to miss. Thirteen defaults did not match their formats’ labels ("998: UNKNOWN" for "998: Unknown", "97: Unknown" for the WKGRPHLA code "998: Unknown"), and five SRLSTT variables (CMV, EBV and hepatitis B results) had their labelled codes replaced by raw ones (#19).
